candidates.name: Joule Capital Partners Utah campus gas interconnection to Kern River
candidates.researcher_notes: Joule Capital Partners applied to Millard County, Utah, for a development agreement to build a 24-inch natural gas transmission pipeline from the Holden area to the McCornick area. The county planning commission notice is for a hearing on May 7, 2026. The notice does not name the data center or Kern River. Holden is where Kern River's mainline runs near the Delta Lateral tap. A Cleanview profile of the Joule data center campus from January 2026 says the campus will connect to the Kern River mainline through redundant 36-inch interconnections, so the tie to the campus comes from that profile and the applicant being the campus developer. The county notice says 24-inch and the profile says 36-inch, so it is not certain these are the same line. Length was not found and no route was found. Status is proposed because no approval or construction was found. Operator not found. Owner name not in the owner list. Separate from the Kern River Delta Lateral (P3856). [QC] independent=yes claimed on 6 surviving ref(s) from 0 publisher(s) -> no.

candidates.name: Nexus Fulcrum Lateral
candidates.monitor_reason: No pipeline sponsor, length, or route is identified for the lateral itself, and it cannot be told apart from the Tahoe Reno Industrial Center spur of the Great Basin 2028 Expansion (P7860). The only concrete step is a power plant application, not a pipeline filing. No data center tie is stated for the pipe.
candidates.researcher_notes: A June 2026 New Project Media article says Nexus Fulcrum LLC applied on June 17 to the Public Utilities Commission of Nevada for a 510 MW gas plant at the former Fulcrum BioEnergy site in the Tahoe Reno Industrial Center, Storey County. It says gas would come through a new lateral connecting to the Great Basin Pipeline system. It also says the plant would serve one customer in the park and support expanded development there, including data centers. The article does not give the lateral's length, route, owner, or diameter, and says the developer and its link to Switch are unclear. A June 2026 Hoodline article describes the Great Basin 2028 Expansion, filed at the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, which includes a spur into the same industrial center. Hoodline is low weight and cites the wrong docket. It is not known whether the plant lateral is that spur, a separate line, or a short in-fence connection. The existing row P7860 already covers the spur. Data center field left blank because no source ties this specific pipe to a data center. Re-check when the Nevada commission docket or Great Basin filings state the lateral's length and owner.

candidates.name: STAK Energy Campus Gas Pipeline
candidates.monitor_reason: no concrete step and no endpoints: the state land lease application covers only the campus site, the pipeline is not part of it, and neither route, length nor gas source is set
candidates.researcher_notes: STAK Energy has applied to the Alaska Division of Oil and Gas for a 50-year lease on about 715 acres near Dalton Highway milepost 390, roughly 26 road miles south of Deadhorse, for a campus of up to 3 gigawatts. A DatacenterDynamics article from May 2026 and a Petroleum News story from June 2026 both say the campus would be fed by new gas pipelines that are still being planned, from fields about 25 to 90 miles away. The pipeline is not part of the lease application and would need its own approval. No route, length, diameter, owner of the pipe or gas supplier has been named. This is not an existing GEM row: the nearby North Slope rows are long-haul or Point Thomson lines with different endpoints. The data center tie is clear, so DataCenter would be yes once a pipeline is formally proposed. Watch for a pipeline right-of-way application, a gas supply deal, or an engineering award. Not found: any permit filing or contract for the pipeline itself. [QC] independent=yes claimed on 1 surviving ref(s) from 0 publisher(s) -> no.

candidates.name: Stratos Project Ruby Pipeline Lateral
candidates.monitor_reason: no concrete step for the lateral itself: the Utah development agreement only allows a gas service deal with Tallgrass, no signed gas contract, filing, or tender found; length and endpoints unknown
candidates.researcher_notes: This is not an existing row. The Ruby Gas Pipeline row (P0248) is the mainline only. The Stratos campus is a data center project in Hansel Valley, Box Elder County, Utah, with a stated plan for gas from the Ruby Pipeline, which crosses the valley. A June 2026 LandGate article says the original plan was on-site gas generation drawing on Ruby, and that the governor then said the campus would never run solely on gas. The first phase is now described as 1 to 1.5 gigawatts of gas with other sources later. Press reports say the April 2026 development agreement lets the developer arrange gas service from Tallgrass Energy through a connection to Ruby. That is permission, not a signed gas contract, a filing or a construction award. No length, route, diameter or capacity for a lateral was found, and the connection may be a short tap. A data center tie exists, so there is no length floor, but the add threshold is not met. Do not tag Ruby (P0248) as a data center line. A Baxtel listing and an Energy Mix article repeat the Ruby gas plan but were not used as refs (Baxtel gave no readable pipeline text, Energy Mix blocked access). Watch for a Tallgrass or Ruby connection filing, a Utah air permit naming a gas line, or a signed gas service agreement.
